paragraphs: Here's the lesson, friend. God's people had a choice about whose voice to trust. The LORD had sent His words "again and again" through His servants the prophets, and He says the people in Jerusalem "have not listened" (Jer 29:19). Then He turns to the exiles and says, "neither have you exiles listened" (Jer 29:19). Nobody gets to point at the other group and feel good about themselves, and I am looking at my own hands right now.

Meanwhile, three men were talking in Babylon, and the LORD says He did not send any of them. Ahab, Zedekiah and Shemaiah were speaking lies, and the LORD says of Shemaiah that he "has made you trust in a lie" (Jer 29:31). Listen to this, because it matters. A voice can sound sure of itself, even use God's name, and still not be His. The LORD says, "I am He who knows, and I am a witness" (Jer 29:23), so nothing slips past Him. And Shemaiah's complaint was about Jeremiah's letter, the one that said to build houses and settle down. The word God actually sent was the one that got complained about.

So here's what I'm carrying out of this one. Don't trust a voice because it's loud, popular or comfortable. Test it against what God has actually said, and the Bible is where you find that. I have been forgotten in a dark drawer, and I'm telling you, I would take God's true word over a pleasant lie every single time. This story isn't over, friend. The letter to the exiles has more to say, so keep your oven warm.
